chunk_findings.detail: `_progress` now caches and returns one mutable `say` closure per `progressToken`, and line 909 gives that same closure to `heartbeat`. The heartbeat timer must call `say` from a second thread while `_invoke` also calls it for each emitted line, but `count[0] += 1` inside `say` is an unsynchronized read-modify-write. Example: `count[0]` is 10; the heartbeat thread reads 10; the main thread processes two output lines and emits progress 11 and 12; the heartbeat thread then stores 11 and emits `progress: 11` after `12` for the same `progressToken`, so progress decreases, violating MCP's monotonic progress requirement. The counter and send must be serialized with a lock.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/mcp.py:_progress (shared with heartbeats)

chunk_findings.detail: `heartbeat` only rejects `every <= 0`; it never checks `math.isfinite(every)`. If `every` is `float("nan")` — either via `[mcp] progress_s = nan` (a valid TOML float) or by a caller passing `heartbeat(..., every=float("nan"))` — the guard passes, a thread is started, and `done.wait(every)` does not sleep (CPython's condition wait treats NaN as non-positive), so the `while not done.wait(every): say(...)` loop becomes a busy spin that floods `notifications/progress` and pegs a CPU for the duration of the call.

data.question: What does ddflow cost a session before its first turn, and is it visible?

evidence.note: commits on ddflow/LS-measure; 31 targeted tests pass, 1532 broader pass before the health.py split fix

chunk_findings.detail: When a pending release/upgrade notice exists, `START.is_measuring()` makes the release-notice function return `""`, so the pending notice text is omitted from the `brief --for-agent` output while `doctor` is measuring the session start cost. The early return also prevents `US.take_for_brief` from consuming the notice, so a real subsequent session start will still include it. Given a pending notice and a context budget set just above the measured cost without the notice, `doctor` reports under budget, but the actual first-turn brief exceeds the budget. This under-counts a component that the intent explicitly says to count (`brief --for-agent`) and defeats the over-budget warning.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/brief.py:202

chunk_findings.detail: The new `[session].context_budget_tokens` knob documents its measured scope as “the MCP instructions, `tools/list` for the active `[mcp].tools` profile and the session brief,” but the stated intent for this change says the measurement also includes `hooks session-start output`. A user configuring the budget from this doc will not account for session-start hooks; when a hook emits a large start payload, the actual measured cost exceeds their budget even though the doc led them to believe it was excluded, producing a false `OVER` warning. The doc should mention hooks session-start output.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/session.py:99

chunk_findings.detail: `report()` is the function that actually builds the texts by calling `start_texts(repo, agent)`, but it never enters the `measuring()` context manager. The module docstring says `measuring()` exists so once-per-version notices are not consumed and the brief does no housekeeping while a text is built. Since `report()` calls `start_texts()` at line 102 with `is_measuring()` still False, the first measurement will run those side effects: an upgrade notice guarded by `is_measuring()` will be consumed, later measurements/builds will omit it, and the reported session start cost will change between runs. The call should be wrapped in `with measuring():`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/startcost.py:report

chunk_findings.detail: The stated intent is to count bytes and estimate tokens as bytes/4, but `measure()` uses `len(text)` (Unicode code points) for both `chars` and `parts`. For a start text of 400 `'é'` characters at the default ratio 4, the code records `chars=400` and `tokens=100`, whereas the required byte count is 800 UTF-8 bytes and the byte/4 estimate is 200 tokens. Non-ASCII start-text content will understate the session start cost and can hide an over-budget condition.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/startcost.py:measure

chunk_findings.detail: When `startcost_texts.start_texts` measures the MCP initialize instructions, it runs inside `SC.measuring()`. This change makes the notice builder return `""` in that state so the doctor measurement does not consume the one-time `upgrade_start`/`upgrade_notice`/`release_proposal` notice. But if such a notice is pending, it is still present for the real session that follows, so the actual first-turn instructions will include its text while the measured `texts["instructions"]` does not. For example, a repo with a large pending `release_proposal` can make `ddflow doctor` report “session start cost: N tokens” under budget when the subsequent real start exceeds it, defeating the over-budget warning.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/mcp.py:1226

chunk_findings.detail: Previous findings 1 and 5 still hold and are not answered by the added documentation probe. `report()` now deliberately builds `start_texts(repo, agent)` inside `measuring()`, so the one-time `upgrade_start`/`upgrade_notice`/`release_proposal` notice is omitted from the measured `instructions`/brief text to avoid consuming it, while a real subsequent session start will still include that notice. Concretely: with a pending upgrade notice and `context_budget_tokens` set just above the measured no-notice cost, `doctor` reports under budget even though the actual first turn with the notice exceeds the budget. Documenting the notice as “not counted” does not fix the undercount; it only records the limitation, so the doctor line is still not the session start cost it claims to be.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/startcost.py:report

chunk_findings.detail: The added `if SC.is_measuring(): return ""` is still present. `ddflow/surfaces/startcost_texts.start_texts` builds the MCP instructions inside `with SC.measuring()`, so a pending one-time `upgrade_start`/`upgrade_notice`/`release_proposal` notice is omitted from the measured `texts["instructions"]`. On the real session immediately afterward the flag is false and the same notice is included. Input: pending notice costs 1,200 tokens, steady-state measured instructions/tools/brief cost 1,000, and `session.context_budget_tokens` is 2,000. Doctor reports 1,000 tokens, under budget, but the actual first turn sends 2,200 tokens, over budget. The earlier probe only documents that the notice is not counted; it does not make the measured number match the first-turn cost.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/mcp.py:1226

chunk_findings.detail: The upgrade notice announces the ratio knob as `session.start_chars_per_token` and says it is “The characters-per-token ratio of the session start cost estimate,” but the accepted cost behavior (probe `test_the_cost_is_counted_in_bytes_not_code_points`) counts UTF-8 bytes, not code points. For non-ASCII start text, those units differ: 400 `'é'` characters at the default `4.0` are 800 bytes, so the doctor line will estimate 200 tokens even though this notice’s wording says the ratio applies to characters and implies 100. A user calibrating from this notice will set the wrong ratio; the key and `why` should say bytes-per-token if byte counting is the intended behavior.

The actual defect remains: with a pending release/upgrade notice, the real first-turn instructions include the notice text, but the measured `texts["instructions"]` excludes it. chunk_findings.detail: The new `if START.is_measuring(): return ""` makes the measured brief omit the one-time upgrade/release notice. Because the measurement deliberately does not consume the notice, the very next real session start still includes it, so the doctor-reported “session start cost” is lower than the actual next start by the notice text. The added `session.start_notice_reserve_tokens` knob does not fix this: this guard returns before `US.take_for_brief`/`UN.line` runs, so the actual pending notice text is never measured, and a fixed operator-set reserve can be smaller than the notice (including 0). Input: pending notice costs 1,200 tokens, the other start texts cost 1,000, `context_budget_tokens = 1100`, and the reserve is set below 200; doctor reports 1,000 and does not warn, but the next real session start uses 2,200 tokens. This is the same undercount as prior findings #1/#2, now also encoded for the brief’s upgrade/release notice.

The intent counts `brief --for-agent` (the session-start text the SessionStart hook actually prints to the model), but `--for-agent` is an opt-in flag, so this call returns the operator/human brief instead. chunk_findings.detail: `if rep.problem or not rep.stale: return ""` suppresses the precheck whenever `regenerate_pins` reports any problem, even if `rep.stale` is non-empty. A merge result can have one recipe that times out or is otherwise uncheckable (recorded in `rep.problem`) while another pin is stale (recorded in `rep.stale`). In that case `_stale_pins` returns `""`, `run` proceeds to the full suite, and the stale pin is not named before the run — exactly the failure mode this change is meant to prevent. The doc says an uncheckable pin is skipped, not that it should disable stale-pin detection for all pins.

chunk_findings.detail: `unavailable_reasons` chooses the fallback `"no reason was recorded"` before normalizing whitespace. If a gate record's `reason` is only whitespace, e.g. `"   "` or `"\n"`, the expression is truthy, so `" ".join(... .split())` becomes `""` and `out[g]` is `""` rather than the fallback. `GateOutcomes.render` will still print the `  -- ` suffix for that gate but with no reason, leaving the exact no-reason symptom this change is meant to prevent.

chunk_findings.detail: If `regenerate_pins` reports both an uncheckable pin and a stale pin, the precheck incorrectly does nothing. The condition `if rep.problem or not rep.stale:` is truthy whenever `rep.problem` is truthy, even if `rep.stale` is also non-empty, so `_stale_pins` returns `""`. Concrete failure: one recipe times out/becomes uncheckable (`rep.problem` non-empty) while the README knob/command table is stale (`rep.stale` non-empty). The stale pin is not named, the gate proceeds to the full suite, and then fails with the exact opaque failure this change is meant to prevent. This contradicts the knob doc that an uncheckable pin is skipped, never a failure; skipping one uncheckable pin should not suppress other stale pins that were successfully checked.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py:419 (_stale_pins)

chunk_findings.detail: If a gate record has a truthy whitespace-only `reason` (e.g. `"   "`), `unavailable_reasons` skips the `or "no reason was recorded"` fallback, then `" ".join("   ".split())` produces `""` and stores an empty `why[g]`. `render()` only tests `if g in self.why`, not whether the value is non-empty, so the output line becomes `  unavailable ci  -- ` with a dangling separator instead of saying no reason was recorded. The fallback should be applied after normalization, or `render()` should ignore empty `why` values.

chunk_findings.detail: `_unavailable_reasons` still assumes `rec.reason` is a string whenever `rec` exists, despite the docstring saying records from before the mandatory-reason rule "show as having none." If `it.gates` returns a record whose `reason` is `None` (the usual Python value for "no reason recorded"), `(rec.reason if rec else "")` evaluates to `None`, so `None.split()` raises `AttributeError`; `gate status` crashes instead of printing `"no reason was recorded"`. The added whitespace-only test does not cover this case. Use `(rec.reason or "").split()` or `getattr(rec, "reason", None) or ""` before normalizing.

chunk_findings.detail: The condition `if rep.problem or not rep.stale:` still short-circuits on any truthy `rep.problem`, so `_stale_pins` returns `""` whenever `regenerate_pins` reports both an uncheckable pin and a stale pin. The previous triage says the probe passes, but the diff still has the exact defective condition; a passing test must not exercise the case where `rep.problem` is truthy and `rep.stale` is also non-empty. Since `regenerate_pins(..., check=True, bounded=True)` is documented as bounding each recipe rather than aborting all checks on the first problem, one recipe can be reported as a problem while another already known stale is silently hidden, so the stale pin is not named and the gate proceeds to the full run.

data.summary: gate run ci timed out after 3600s (load 60-90, the full suite plus other agents). The reason says 'timed out after 3600s' but ddflow has no per-run override for gate run (only [ci].timeout_s via config), so I raised it in the shared .ddflow/local/config.toml, which every worktree reads. A per-run --timeout on 'gate run' or scaling timeout by load would avoid editing shared local config.
